dod_intent_evidence: Air Force SBIR Phase II 2022 ($750K) building 5G-ARES for AFSOC's 361st ISRG ('This project will immediately support the mission of the 361st ISRG' — SBIR abstract), plus a 2021 DHS Phase II for C-UAS (news); site sells the CNG sensor explicitly for 'Defense and ISR'.
score_evidence: 'Best-in-class survey speed' / 'real time' repeated across every capability block — spec brags with tactical adjectives but no operational depth → lab_language_intensity

'Fully automated. Self-configuring... Low-drag user experience and mission-ready performance' — marketing-tactical, never a word on ATO, STIGs, ITAR, or how the data legally reaches a mission network → deployment_awareness_absence
No mention anywhere of who operates, trains on, or maintains the CNG2440 in the field; 'low-drag user experience' is the closest they come → operator_absence
No jobs data in pack — hiring_profile_skew set to exactly 10 per rule

Phase II awarded 2022, period of performance long expired; 3-7 employees and (aggregator estimate, Blitz/LI) ~$631.7K annual revenue with no follow-on contract news since — the classic post-Phase-II stall → stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Your stack, your way' integration hand-waving in place of platform-integration reality
blind_spots.operator_reality: Mounting a 2U emitter-adjacent RF sensor on an aircraft or vessel means GFE integration, EMI/EMC and safety-of-flight sign-off, and prime-led subcontract flow-down — 'standard data streams and formats' gets a demo flight, not a fielded fit. The months those approvals take are exactly the months a $750K Phase II doesn't fund.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: A 3-7 person RF engineering team that has lived in survey and test environments, not through a prime's airworthiness and integration gauntlet.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Deploy across airborne, ground, and maritime platforms via standard data streams and formats. Your stack, your way.

blind_spots.blind_spot: A situational-awareness sensor with no TAK/CoT story
blind_spots.operator_reality: The product exists to give AFSOC 'direct threat warning and enhanced situational awareness', yet nothing in their language mentions ATAK/TAK or Cursor-on-Target output — meaning the network laydown lives on the sensor's own 'on-board display and UI' while the operators it warns are looking at ATAK. A geolocation feed that can't hit the common operating picture doesn't change anyone's decision.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Cellular-RF specialists optimizing detection and decode; the consumption side of the intelligence loop is someone else's problem until transition dies for lack of it.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: A complete signal-to-intelligence loop, in a single sensor.

blind_spots.blind_spot: No ATO/accreditation path for the intelligence the sensor produces
blind_spots.operator_reality: Passive collection against '5G NR and 4G LTE' generates data that must land on accredited government networks (and much of it at classification); without an RMF ATO, STIGged software, and an IL-rated transport path, the CNG2440's output legally stops at the transit case. 'Fully automated, self-configuring' software with no compliance language is a demo-only system on a government range.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The Phase II funded sensor performance, not cyber accreditation; nobody on a team this size owns RMF paperwork.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Real-time passive collection. Detection, decoding, geolocation. Fully automated, self-configuring.

opener_hook: Cobalt's 5G-ARES Phase II for AFSOC's 361st ISRG was awarded in 2022 — three years on, the CNG2440 page promises 'your stack, your way' but names no TAK output, no ATO path, and no transition vehicle, which is where 2U sensors go quiet.
what_they_do: Austin micro-team (3-7 people) building the CNG2440, a 2U ruggedized sensor that detects, decodes, and geolocates 4G/5G cellular networks from ground, air, and maritime platforms.
